method: Flesch Kincaid grade plus five, using a vowel-group syllable heuristic. Punctuated sentences and standalone task lines are counted as sentence units. Exact corpora and hashes retained. Numeric price table fragments, headings, staff text, dates, lesson codes and the verbatim scheme outcome are excluded. Estimates guide editing; they are not learner assessments. Read-aloud and confirmed scribing routes are available.

A balanced eating pattern uses a variety of food groups. The meal you design is one part of what someone eats over time.
The two largest groups in a balanced eating pattern are vegetables and fruit, and starchy foods. Include protein foods and dairy or suitable alternatives. Use small amounts of oils and spreads. Balance is built across the day or week; every meal does not need exact plate sections. Choose water as a drink. No calorie counting, weight talk or food judgement is needed.
The quantities in this pack are classroom planning examples. Appetite and individual needs vary. These examples do not set a diet or a nutritional target for each pupil.

Plan one meal for one person. Your ingredient-use budget is £2.00.
All prices are invented for this lesson. Each price covers the stated amount for one person. These are ingredient-use costs, not the cost of buying whole packs. No spending or shopping is required. Water is available at no charge in this classroom model.
Use one price for each listed quantity. Half of a listed quantity costs half its price in this model. If a suitable replacement is not on the card, ask the adult to provide and record a new invented price before costing it.
No oil is added to the model wrap. The yoghurt is shared between the filling and the side serving, so charge its 60 g cost once.

Cold bean and vegetable wrap with fruit and plain yoghurt
For one person. Use the listed amounts. Total ingredient-use cost £1.40. No heat is required. This week, choose and rehearse the method. Prepare food only in the later supervised practical.
With adult approval, wash the vegetables and fruit. Grate the carrot and finely slice the cabbage using the agreed tools. An adult can prepare these for you.
Use 80 g of ready-to-eat cooked beans, drained by an adult if needed. Mash with a fork. Mix in about 20 g of the plain yoghurt and the vegetables.
Put the filling on the wrap. Fold it. Serve with the washed fruit and the rest of the yoghurt. Keep it chilled until eaten and follow the adult’s plan.
An adult opens tins and removes sharp lids before the activity. Use the approved allergy and access plan. Tasting is optional. Clean and clear the station at the end.

Keep this card with your meal plan for the next supervised lesson. Ask the adult before handling any food or tool.
Tell the adult about dietary and access needs privately. The adult checks every ingredient label and the agreed allergy plan before ingredients are issued.
Wash hands with soap and water before food preparation, after the toilet and after touching waste. Dry them well. Tie hair back, cover cuts and clean the work surface and tools.
Use knives, graters and open tins only with adult approval and supervision. Keep fingers away from sharp edges. Ask for pre-cut vegetables or adult help.
Use beans labelled cooked and ready to eat. Dry beans need a different cooking process and are not used here. Keep ready-to-eat food away from raw food.
Keep chilled ingredients at 5°C or below, follow use-by dates and storage labels, and take out only what you need. The adult handles storage and any leftovers.
Tasting is optional. Never share a tasting spoon. If anything spills, breaks or feels unsafe, stop, put the tool down and tell the adult. Clear and clean using the agreed routine.
This model uses a wrap that contains wheat including gluten, and yoghurt that contains milk. Every actual ingredient still needs a label check. Soya is in the optional alternative. Tell the adult privately about needs. Tasting is your choice.
